results.answer: A Merkle tree (hash tree) is a tree in which each leaf node is labelled with the cryptographic hash of a data block and each non-leaf node with the hash of its children's labels, allowing efficient and secure verification of the contents of a large data structure, such as confirming that data blocks received from peers are undamaged and unaltered or that a leaf belongs to the tree.

results.answer: A Merkle tree is a hierarchical hash structure in which each leaf node holds the cryptographic hash of a data block and each internal node is labeled with the hash of its children, allowing efficient and secure verification that a specific data block is part of a larger commitment.

limitations: Three unique public reading questions repeated twice, not a production browser-automation qualification.
Actual frontier API usage/cost; replayed worker packets with earlier measured worker cost. Composite latency is additive, not a fresh integrated latency measurement.
Main model is metered Claude Opus5.5 via OpenRouter, not this Codex session. No assertion about Codex/ChatGPT credit conversion.
All frontier requests reported zero cached input tokens in this sample; real cached sessions may save less money.
Local compute cost is not priced; two local-Jev Merkle answers propagated a factual error.
Full-source baseline is bounded to32000characters; Bloom-filter page has66256characters. Shared prompt/instructions match across lanes, but worker summaries contain less detail.
